Every record carries a hidden sys_domain field:

  Subsidiary A's domain    Subsidiary B's domain
  - incidents, catalog     - incidents, catalog
  - never visible to B     - never visible to A
       \                        /
        \__ parent/top domain __/
           (sees across both)
caption: One shared instance, walled-off data, no second production instance needed.

code:
Subsidiaries under one parent:          MSP serving multiple clients:
- shared instance for licensing/         - Client X and Client Y on the
  operations efficiency                     same tables, same scoped apps
- A's data never visible to B            - each client's data invisible
  (or vice versa)                            to the other, always
caption: Genuinely separate entities with a non-negotiable requirement that data never cross.

code:
Domain-separated:                     Domain-extendable:
- visible only within its own         - top domain can see AND edit
  domain, never a sibling's               records in subordinate domains
- Client X cannot see Client Y's      - MSP admin manages shared
  incidents, ever                         configuration centrally
caption: Getting this choice wrong is how data leaks, or shared config becomes unmanageable.
